neighbours.label: news-style attribution of a claim to a generic or unnamed expert source ('a recent study shows', 'one analyst says', 'according to a leading astronomer', 'sources say'); named characters' speech in narrative does not fire
fire: Rising sea levels will swamp the delta within decades, according to one climate scientist.
The merger is unlikely to clear regulators, a banking analyst told the paper.
Nearly half of the bridges are overdue for repair, a new report finds.
One former official said the agency had ignored the warnings for years.
Sleep loss blunts memory even in healthy adults, researchers say.
The stadium deal makes no financial sense, one economist argues.
The outbreak likely began in a single market, a health expert says.
Sources close to the deal say the price could reach two billion.
quiet: Rising sea levels will swamp the delta within decades, Tom told his daughter on the walk home.
The merger is unlikely to clear regulators, she muttered to herself at the bus stop.
Nearly half of the bridges are overdue for repair, the sign on the gate warned.
My uncle said the shop had ignored the complaints for years.
Sleep loss blunts memory, Anna reminded her brother at breakfast.
The stadium deal makes no sense, Grandpa grumbled over his newspaper.
We study the outbreak in class every Tuesday and read a chapter aloud.
Close to the deadline, the price rose to two billion.
